page: Microsoft Azure FX8mds_v2 is a high-frequency, memory-dense virtual machine within Azure's compute-optimized FX family. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by a dedicated 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8573C processor presenting 4 physical cores and 8 vCPUs with hyperthreading enabled. It features a substantial 260 MB L3 cache alongside advanced vector extensions, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX instructions. The instance is configured with an extensive 168.0 GB of memory, resulting in an unusually high allocation of 21.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage includes a 472 GB local NVMe SSD, while no discrete GPUs are bundled.

In benchmark assessments, the FX8mds_v2 exhibits top-tier single-threaded performance driven by its 4.2 GHz clock speed and large cache hierarchy. It reaches a Geekbench single-core score of 2361.0 and achieves strong single-threaded data compression, recording 34.97 GB/sec in gzip compression and 14.45 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. The CPU architecture also demonstrates high efficiency on small-model inference tasks, processing 344.1 tokens/sec for text generation with a 135M parameter LLM. Conversely, multi-threaded throughput across PassMark (15813.59) and stress-ng (8890.65) falls within average percentiles, bounded by the 8-vCPU ceiling. Medium-scale language model generation (7B) also slows to 8.5 tokens/sec, highlighting CPU execution boundaries compared to dedicated accelerator hardware.

From an operational and cost-efficiency perspective, the FX8mds_v2 provides substantial memory density combined with dedicated high-frequency cores, avoiding resource contention common in shared architectures. The inclusion of fast local NVMe storage reduces external disk I/O dependency for temporary scratch space. This profile is suited for memory-bound, single-thread-intensive workloads such as in-memory databases, electronic design automation (EDA), compilation pipelines, and financial modeling applications requiring high per-core execution speeds and expansive RAM capacity.
